items.text:
Most founders don't have a revenue problem. They have a timing problem.

You invoiced $80k in March. It landed in May. Payroll didn't wait.

Three habits fixed this for our customers:
1. Look at cash weekly, not monthly.
2. Chase invoices at day 7, not day 45.
3. Know your runway in weeks.

Boring? Yes. That's the point.

Your month-end close is slow because it's a ritual, not a process.

We watched 140 small businesses close their books. The slow ones weren't worse at accounting. They had 40 tiny manual steps nobody had questioned in years.

Automate the boring 30. Keep a human on the 10 that need judgment.

A customer asked me on Tuesday: "Can we afford a second hire?"

Two years ago that question took two weeks and three spreadsheets. This time it took ten minutes, because their books were closed on the 3rd.

Fast books aren't about accounting. They're about decisions.

Cash flow is really important for small businesses. Many founders struggle with it. It's important to keep track of your finances and plan ahead. Having good bookkeeping helps a lot. Make sure you review your numbers regularly and work with good partners.

Bookkeeping. It matters. Do it. Thanks for reading and follow for more.

Hot take: the best finance teams I know are a little boring.

Same checklist every Monday. Same owner for every account. Same day for every close.

Boring is what lets them say yes quickly when something exciting shows up.
